title: Decoupled KV Proxies and Quorum-Aware Partitioning
content:
Overview

Goal: propose a hybrid multi-GPU serving approach that separates KV cache responsibilities from token routing and collective/kernel coordination. Instead of tightly coupling KV ownership to GPU shard placement, introduce lightweight local KV proxies (one per host or per GPU-NUMA domain) that provide a quorum-aware partitioning layer. This document is intentionally exploratory — tradeoffs, benchmarks, and backwards-compatibility items listed below.

Motivation / problem statement
- Current tight KV->shard binding causes expensive resharding and backpressure when node topology changes (preemptions, reprovisioning, heterogeneous fleets).
- NCCL tuning and collective schedules are brittle when KV ownership is moving; small kv-population churn amplifies all-reduce noise and latency spikes.
- We want predictable tail latency while maintaining high utilization across multi-tenant GPU pools.

Key idea
- Introduce a thin KV proxy layer that:
  - front-ends get/set/evict requests for KV entries (activation prefixes, cached past keys/values)
  - maintains a soft partitioning map (hash->proxy endpoints) with quorum semantics (R/W quorums)
  - coordinates with serving runtime to prefetch and pin hot prefixes to local GPU memory when workload signals it
- Serve runtime keeps token routing, microbatch scheduling, kernel selection, and NCCL collective orchestration; proxies handle cache availability and consistency.

Design components
1) KV proxy placement
   - Option A: host-level proxy (one per physical host). Pros: fewer proxies, easier quorum. Cons: cross-host network hop for GPU-local accesses.
   - Option B: GPU-NUMA-level proxy (one per GPU or per GPU socket). Pros: lower host-local latency and avoids PCIe crosses for cached hits. Cons: more proxies => more metadata and heartbeats.
   - Default recommendation: host-level proxy for initial alpha; allow per-GPU proxy as opt-in for high-density nodes.

2) Partitioning and quorum semantics
   - Partition space: consistent-hash on prefix fingerprint (sha1-64 or xxhash64) -> vnode map.
   - Replication factor: configurable RF (default 3) across proxies located in same region/zone.
   - Read quorum R = 1 or 2 depending on strong/weak consistency lease. Write quorum W = majority (ceil(RF/2)+1) for safe update path.
   - Cache insertion: warm path writes to primary then replicates asynchronously to secondaries; can optionally use write-through to backing storage for cold fetches.

3) Eviction / TTL / Hotset mechanics
   - Each proxy maintains an LFU-ish score + moving-average access time per prefix.
   - Global hotset hints: serving runtime emits periodic hotset heartbeat (top-K prefixes observed local to the GPU in last N seconds). Proxies prioritize those for pinning.
   - Eviction policy must coordinate with microbatching heuristics: evicting a prefix currently in-flight is allowed only if pinned lifetimes expired or preemptive migration occurs.

4) Prefetching and pinning protocol
   - When a request arrives on the serving runtime for a prefix and proxy returns miss, the runtime can issue a prefetch RPC to the proxy with a pin TTL (short, e.g., 500ms - 5s) depending on predicted sequence length.
   - Pin request: proxy fetches (from replica or backing store), loads into local NVRAM or GPU-mapped buffer, returns a pin token. Runtime attaches token to microbatch to avoid eviction until token expiry.

5) Interaction with NCCL and kernel scheduling
   - Keep NCCL collectives aligned with shard placement. The proxy layer should expose a lightweight placement hint API to the orchestrator: "prefix X is hot on proxy P1,P2". Orchestrator can prefer placement of this model shard (or keep it replicated) to minimize cross-host traffic.
   - NCCL ramp-up strategy (novel): when a GPU group first forms, use an adaptive ramp-up window to warm all-reduce sizes. Instead of immediate full-size all-reduces, use staged collectives: small-value aggregation -> progressive fusion -> full collectives. This reduces latency tail for ephemeral groups.
   - Proof-of-concept tuning knobs: initial-chunk-size (KB), fusion-threshold (tokens), background-chunking-rate. These interact with proxy prefetch latency — proxies should expose instantaneous hit/miss rate metrics.

Operational considerations
- Failure modes: proxy outage -> serving runtime falls back to direct backing-store fetches or to degraded single-shard KV with increased NCCL cross-node traffic. Need clear SLA and circuit-breaker.
- Split-brain: quorum semantics prevent stale reads; membership changes require rebalancing with an overlap window to avoid read anomalies.
- Migration plan: incremental deploy: host-proxy mode behind feature flag; monitor hit-rate and tail-latency for a few persistent models.

Benchmarks to run (initial experiments)
1) Baseline: current tight-KV binding (no proxies) with 8xA100, 4 GPUs/node, batch mix: 70% short (1-64 tokens), 30% long (65-2048 tokens). Collect p50/p90/p99 latency and token cost.
2) Host-proxy RF=3, R=1, W=2, compare tail latency and NCCL traffic (bytes per second between GPUs) while increasing preemption noise (kill 1 node every 30s).
3) Proxy placement compare: host-level vs per-GPU on dense nodes (16 GPUs). Measure miss penalty and network hops.
4) Ramp-up vs naive NCCL start strategy: measure p99 during group churn.

Checklist / TODOs
- [ ] Build lightweight proxy binary (go/rust) with in-memory index and backing S3-like fetcher. PR: see linked_artifacts PR 4821.
- [ ] Implement pin token API in serving runtime; ensure token follows microbatch lifecycle.
- [ ] Add metrics: proxy.hit_rate, proxy.latency_ms_p95, proxy.mem_pressure, proxy.replicas_in_sync_percent.
- [ ] Create Canary: enable proxies for one small dedicated capacity pool and run for 2 weeks.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should we prefer eventual consistency with R=1 for reads to reduce latency, or keep R=2 for safer semantics? Recommendation: R=1 for hosted API by default, allow stronger semantics for enterprise/private deployments.
- How costly is per-GPU proxy in practice with 1M prefix keys? Memory and heartbeat scaling need measurement.
- Interaction with model rollouts: when model version changes, how to invalidate pinned prefixes deterministically without stalling live traffic? Proposed: versioned prefix keyspace and lazy eviction on first mismatch.

Notes to self
- Remember to coordinate with observability (Priya) for logging format: include prefix-fingerprint, pin-token-id, and serving-route in spans.
- Sync with SRE (Jonah) on failure-mode runbook and automated fallback to direct fetch.

References
- CON-9321: KV proxy architecture exploration (Confluence)
- GitHub PR 4821: initial proxy binary prototype

If this doc lands in a design review, focus discussion on: quorum choice, proxy placement default, and NCCL ramp-up knobs. Keep design conservative for alpha and emphasize incremental rollout paths.
